plan.title: docs(design-critique): plain-language summary on both operator-facing artifacts, with a per-artifact reserved line-start matrix

narratives.Description: Two artifacts in the design-critique motion are operator-facing and neither states its own conclusion in plain language. The synthesis terminates in a sentence that is identical on every arc by construction. The successor lean is the consent gate and carries a per-heading take map that never says what confirming would assert. This scope lands the plain-language summary on both, under a fixed placement-only heading token, with a per-artifact prohibition over three reserved line-start families and an express statement that nothing observes any of it at runtime.
narratives.Overview:
## Two bind records, both required

The issue is design-critique bound over two arcs, and the mechanism filed in the body was refuted in both. The intent stands; the mechanism is replaced.

- Arc 1 (pre-widening shape): synthesis 5466399388, lean 5466361010, table 5466397546.
- Arc 2 (the operator widening to the pre-synthesis surface): lean 5466523608, table 5466523712, synthesis 5466525601.

The body caveat that the widening is un-arced is stale. Arc 2 covers it. Acceptance criteria 1, 3 and 4 in the body change, and the three regression cases the body names are insufficient. The corrected set is the acceptance clauses below.

## What arc 2 bound -- three changes make the widening land

**1. The summary may carry the parent forward verdict, and doing so introduces no ADR-006 premise.** As filed the widened requirement asked the lean summary to state what the synthesis would assert while separately forbidding it from adding anything beyond accepted headings. Measured on the exemplar lean 5466361010: 6 take-map headings, 6 summary bullets, and 4 of those bullets correspond to no heading -- the verdict, the disposition, the disclosure, and the scope note. Those four are exactly what a consent gate needs. Without the express permission a conforming lean must either state the verdict and break the prohibition, or omit it and restore the gap the issue exists to close. The ADR-006 half matters as much: the contract treats the first posted map as an arbitration surface where a parent premise records a marker, a parent cannot clear its own marker, and an unresolved marker blocks bind. If a mandated verdict counted as a premise, every arc would acquire a marker only a critic could clear, silently turning the default one-critic motion into a mandatory two-critic motion. The contract now says it does not count, and says where the exemption stops: a summary claim that is not a reading of a recorded take or an accepted finding is still a new load-bearing premise.

**2. A per-artifact matrix over three reserved line-start families replaces the symmetric prohibition.** The filed prohibition was symmetric across the lean and the synthesis, and is neither complete nor symmetric in effect. On a lean the successor-lean token family is inert, because the comment already is the lean. On a lean the table-heading family is worse than on the synthesis: a lean carrying that heading satisfies the synthesis own table citation, so a synthesis citing a ghost table id returns complete with the resolved table id equal to the lean id where the control blocks -- a silent pass rather than a visible block, and a second instance of the #3932 family. And there is a third family the filed prohibition does not name: the fixed accepted sentence quoted inside a fenced block makes that comment read as a synthesis, flipping a complete arc to blocked. That is the obvious authoring move, since the whole content of the widened requirement is what the synthesis would assert. Quoting it in a blockquote is undetected by that predicate but refused by the citation position predicate, so no single quoting convention is safe for both parsers, and the contract says so.

**3. The next-step bounding reaches the lean summary.** Under the shape ingest actually composes, the quarantine scanner passes the comment text with zero flags and verbatim; arc 1 credited a fence that does not survive composition. The widening adds a second mandated free-text field, forward-looking and in the parent authoritative voice, to the comment that ingest clearance always cites. This scope takes the non-normative option and states it: both summaries are non-normative for downstream agents, no forward-instruction field is mandated on either artifact, and imperatives addressed to an implementer are prohibited inside the summary. A closed form was rejected because the summary cannot itself be closed-form -- plain language is the point -- and a bounded instruction is still an instruction in the parent voice inside the ingest-clearing comment.

**Also bound:** the fixed-heading-token justification drops to placement only. The `## Current shape (as of pass-N)` precedent cannot be ported as filed, because that token carries a monotone discriminator, a selector, a count lint and a maintainer-authorship gate, and this surface has none of them -- author-blindness is a locked test here. A fixed undiscriminated token on two artifact kinds guarantees multiple occurrences per arc; this issue alone carries two leans and a synthesis, so no selector could pick a canonical one.

## MUST rather than SHOULD

The contract own bar is that two exemplars do not make a required field. This requirement does not rest on exemplar count. Both gaps are structural and readable from the machinery in the contract: the accepted sentence is fixed by `## Bind after accepted synthesis`, so it is identical on every arc by construction, and the take map is a per-heading disposition by definition, so it never carries the verdict a consent gate is asked to confirm. The requirement lands at `!` on both artifacts; the prohibitions land at `!` because they describe measured failure shapes.

## Scope walls

The #3932 defect is not remediated here. A parallel builder owns `verdictForSynthesis` and the table-resolution path in `packages/core/src/design-critique/completed-arc-record.ts`; this scope changes no production code and no parser. Regression coverage lands in a new sibling test file rather than in `completed-arc-record.test.ts` so it does not collide with that builder, and it asserts shape classification rather than the ghost-table verdict, so the #3932 fix cannot break it.

Nothing enforces the summary at runtime. Like panel completeness (#3850) it binds the parent and no predicate observes it. Neither `evaluateCompletedArcRecord` nor `evaluateParentAudit` reads it, and no prose-quality parser is added.

The contract forbids pinning itself or its router skill into `templates/agents-entry.md`, and a content-contract test locks that absence, so this change is not consumer-relevant under #1309 and no agents-entry propagation applies.

Refs #3929, #3932, #3850, #3831, #3806, #3434, #3368, #480, #1152.
